subject: Request: temporary latency attenuation variance for reserved GPUs
messages:
From: Marta Ruiz <mruiz@solsticehealth.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Cloud Contracts <contracts@solsticehealth.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity: request for temporary latency attenuation variance

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As Solstice scales our clinical transcription and summarization pipelines into peak hours, we continue to see a very wide tail on token latency during cold-start windows and long-context sessions. Our infra leads ran a capture and attached a small CSV with token-percentile measurements for July (redwood-latency-report-202707.csv).

We are coming to renew our 3-node reserved GPU commitment and want to propose a limited SLA amendment: a 6-week latency "attenuation variance" where the agreed tail SLO (99th token latency) has a relaxed threshold during nightly cold windows (02:00-05:00 PT) and during any contiguous workload spikes longer than 10 minutes. In exchange we can increase our committed throughput hours by 25% and accept a 3% uplift on monthly committed spend.

This is not a permanent carveout — it's a temporary tolerance while we iterate on batching and KV-warm strategies on our side. Practical asks:
- Can Redwood provide a formal amendment template we can review with legal?
- Will you confirm what mitigations Redwood can enable server-side (sticky KV caching, proactive pre-warm, short priority tokens) during the period?
- Any impact to incident credits or uptime SLA during the variance?

Attaching the report and a draft amendment from our counsel for context. Happy to jump on a 30-minute call if easier.

Best,
Marta Ruiz
Director, Platform Engineering
Solstice Health

Attachment: redwood-latency-report-202707.csv
Attachment: solstice-draft-amendment-v1.pdf

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Marta Ruiz <mruiz@solsticehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 22 Aug 2027 13:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: request for temporary latency attenuation variance

Hi Marta — thanks for the clear note and the data. Appreciate you proposing a constructive trade (25% extra committed throughput in exchange for a short-term variance).

Quick answers up front:
- We can produce an amendment draft for a temporary latency variance. It will enumerate the time windows, success criteria, rollback triggers, and economics.
- Server-side mitigations we can enable quickly:
  * sticky KV caching for 24-hour affinity on the reserved pool (reduces cold-KV misses)
  * scheduled pre-warm jobs (we can run a pre-warm across the pool in the 30 minutes before your 02:00 window)
  * limited priority tokens for warmup traffic (isolated to your pool/subnet)
  * optional short-lived ephemeral warm nodes for bursty migrations (adds cost while active)

Important caveats: the uptime SLA (monthly availability) remains unchanged; however, incident credits tied specifically to token latency SLOs would be adjusted for the defined windows while the variance is active. We will document this clearly in the amendment.

I will coordinate an internal proposal and loop in Contracts to formalize. Can you confirm the exact three-week start window you're targeting (you mentioned iterating for six weeks — do you want the window to begin 2027-09-01 or earlier)?

If agreeable, I can send a redlined amendment by EOD tomorrow.

— Stephanie
Product Partnerships (Dedicated Capacity)
Redwood Inference

On Sun, Aug 22, 2027 at 09:12 AM Marta Ruiz <mruiz@solsticehealth.com> wrote:
> Hi Stephanie,
> 
> [original message attached]

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 23 Aug 2027 10:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Dedicated capacity: request for temporary latency attenuation variance

Team — forwarding Solstice's request. High-level: they want a 6-week temporary relaxation of the 99th-token latency SLO for narrow windows (nightly 02:00–05:00 PT and spikes >10m) in exchange for a 25% bump in committed throughput and ~+3% monthly commit. They attached latency CSV and a draft amendment.

Questions we need to decide before we send a formal amendment:
1) Do we accept a temporary SLO relaxation in-band with a throughput upsell? If yes, what guardrails (rollback triggers, monitoring thresholds) are mandatory?
2) Which server-side mitigations do we enable by default vs as paid add-ons (sticky KV caching might be free for 30 days, pre-warm jobs are ops-intensive and could be amortized)?
3) Pricing: is the 3% uplift adequate for the additional operational overhead and potential queueing risk for co-located tenants? Ben/david — need rough $ impact ASAP so I can include a line in the amendment.

I recommend: accept the variance with firm rollback triggers (e.g., if overall monthly 99th-latency exceeds baseline+15% outside defined windows, variance auto-revoked), include sticky KV caching for free during the period, price pre-warm and ephemeral warm nodes as opt-in add-ons, and document that uptime SLA is unchanged but latency credits are paused only for the defined windows.

Thoughts?
— Steph

Attachment: redwood-latency-report-202707.csv

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 24 Aug 2027 09:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Dedicated capacity: request for temporary latency attenuation variance

Agree with Steph's approach. Quick pricing math:
- 25% committed throughput on a 3-node reserved pool (current commit $92k/mo) => incremental committed revenue ~ $23k/mo.
- Operational overhead for pre-warm orchestration + SLT on-call ~ $2k/week while active (~$8k over 6 weeks).
- Risk allowance for queueing/carveouts: we should add a buffer line in the amendment that allows us to temporarily impose per-VM concurrency limits if host-level contended bursts threaten other tenants. That buffer should not be used lightly — we'd notify 48 hours in advance.

Recommendation: accept with the financials you proposed, mark pre-warm orchestration as an optional billable service ($4k flat for the 6-week window or $750/week), include a rollback clause tied to cross-tenant latency regressions (as Steph suggested), and provide 14-day notice language for any forced concurrency throttles.

I'll draft the numbers into the amendment and share a pricing appendix.

— Ben

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Marta Ruiz <mruiz@solsticehealth.com>, Cloud Contracts <contracts@solsticehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Aug 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Proposed temporary variance amendment and options (Solstice Health)

Hi Marta / Contracts team,

Thanks for the patience while we pulled together internal approvals. Attached is a short-form amendment (see related link to the internal proposal) that does the following:
- Grants a 6-week temporary latency attenuation variance window starting 2027-09-01 through 2027-10-12, scoped to nightly 02:00–05:00 PT and any contiguous burst >10 minutes defined by token arrival rate > 2x baseline.
- Pauses latency-linked credits for the scoped windows only; the monthly uptime SLA remains unchanged.
- Commits Solstice to +25% committed throughput for the duration; financial appendix reflects a +3% monthly commitment uplift and an optional pre-warm orchestration fee (flat $4k for 6 weeks).
- We will enable sticky KV caching for your reserved pool for the term at no additional charge and offer scheduled pre-warm jobs as an opt-in paid add-on.
- Rollback triggers: if cross-tenant monthly 99th-token latency (outside scoped windows) exceeds historical baseline +15% for two consecutive weeks, Redwood may revoke the variance with 7 days' notice.
- If Redwood must apply temporary per-host concurrency limits to protect other tenants, we will provide at least 14 days' notice unless an emergency is declared.

Next steps:
1) Please review and propose any edits to the narrow windows/thresholds.
2) If you accept economics, Contracts can circulate a DocuSign-ready amendment; otherwise we can schedule a call to walk through the appendix.

Happy to hop on 30 minutes tomorrow if helpful.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Product Partnerships (Dedicated Capacity)
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: redwood-latency-report-202707.csv, proposed-amendment-v1.pdf
DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/solstice/amendment-v1
